source.title: Polysemy of Synthetic Neurons Towards a New Type of Explanatory Categorical Vector Spaces
source.authors: Michael Pichat; William Pogrund; Paloma Pichat; Judicael Poumay; Armanouche Gasparian; Samuel Demarchi; Martin Corbet; Alois Georgeon; Michael Veillet-Guillem

record.tranche_reason: The paper presents an alternative, explicitly non-exclusive account of neuronal polysemy as an intra-neuronal categorical vector space and reports measurements of that account. It does not directly test the standard superposition, capacity-pressure, or SAE claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition and polysemantic neurons, but its own analyses operationalize categorical subdimensions using shared core-tokens and GPT2-XL embedding similarities. These results do not directly measure the feature directions, capacity pressure, or SAE features named by the claim versions. Results cited from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes an intra-neuronal 'categorical vector space' account of neuron polysemy in GPT2-XL layer 1, which the authors explicitly call non-exclusive and compatible with superposition. Its measures come from token-overlap clusters with layer-0 neurons and GPT2-XL input-embedding cosine similarity, related to activation rank. None of them measures feature directions, capacity pressure, sparsity, or SAE features. The results therefore do not bear on whether any version holds. The paper does not argue that polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure; it offers a parallel interpretation. The superposition material is a literature review, so this is discussion rather than a T5 test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that more highly activated core-tokens in GPT2-XL layer-1 neurons are closer to more of the neuron's categorical sub-dimensions, and therefore less polysemantic. They propose modelling a neuron as an intra-neuronal, non-orthogonal categorical vector space, as a non-exclusive alternative to inter-neuronal superposition. The summary says 'first two perceptron layers', but the analyses cover layer-1 neurons, with clusters defined via layer-0 neurons.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes GPT2-XL core-token activation, embedding cosine proximity to shared-token clusters, and PCA; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method or measure its superposition loss/geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are reported for selected layer-1 neuron cohorts with different taken-cluster selection criteria; no cross-layer, model, or prompt comparison is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: In 614 selected GPT2-XL layer-1 neurons, the top-10 core-tokens had higher mean embedding-cosine proximity to taken-clusters than the bottom-10 core-tokens (δ=.0274; 78% of neurons δ>0; Cliff's delta .24). On a 612-neuron averaged neuron, Kendall τ between activation rank and proximity was .78–.85.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a polysemantic MLP neuron, higher-activating tokens lie closer to all of the neuron's input-derived token clusters at once, consistent with a monosemantic top-activation zone.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA over four subdimension-proximity variables (463-neuron averaged neuron): Factor 1 explains 93.5% and is all-positive; Factor 2 explains 4.8% and is contrastive. High-activation tokens sit high on Factor 1 and negative on Factor 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The input-derived token clusters of a neuron are largely non-orthogonal (convergent), with a small divergent (polysemantic) component.

record.problems: The empirical analysis is restricted to GPT2-XL layer 1 and selected core-tokens and taken-clusters. The study’s categorical-subdimension measures are constructed from token overlap and embedding cosine similarity; the results do not independently validate those constructs as the model’s represented features. The authors note that local inferential differences are modest.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or feature importance determining dedicated vs shared dimensions.
An alternative account of polysemy is proposed, but there is no test isolating polysemanticity from capacity pressure. The authors explicitly call their account non-contradictory to superposition.
No measure of features spread across neurons and no dictionary/SAE recovery.
The 'categorical sub-dimensions' are token-cluster constructs, not tests of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly link to 'none'. The caption of Graph 1 appears mislabeled (it refers to layer 0 clusters), though the text describes layer-1 activation-proximity curves. Core-tokens come from the OpenAI Bills et al. 2023 neuron data. Proximity is measured in input-embedding space, not in the model's internal representations. There are no controls (e.g., random clusters or non-core tokens). Many references appear erroneous, e.g. [1] is cited as Haider et al. but the reference is a PennyLang paper.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-sparsity sweep, superposition transition, or regular polytope geometry are tested.
The paper does not test whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The proposed intra-neuronal account is presented as an alternative interpretation, but the study does not test whether polysemanticity arises independently of capacity pressure.
No analysis tests feature distribution across neurons or recovery of sparse features with a dictionary or SAE.
No SAE features are evaluated for completeness, stability, or canonical status.
The paper analyzes categorical subdimensions, not the dimensionality of the features or directions posited by standard superposition accounts.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Compared dimensional proximity of the 10 least- and 10 most-activated core-tokens for each retained layer-1 neuron.

conditions.value: at least 3 taken-clusters, each with at least 6 taken-tokens, and at least 40 distinct tokens across clusters

rows.measure: Mean dimensional proximity to the principal categorical subdimensions; difference between high- and low-activation token groups
rows.note: The paper reports mean αmin = 1.3843 and mean αmax = 3.0218. The reported proximity difference is positive in the predicted direction for the authors’ categorical-subdimension hypothesis.
rows.check: Correct link. The Cliff's delta effect size (.2407, Table 1) could be added to the value.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Counted retained layer-1 neurons with positive dimensional-proximity difference between high- and low-activation token groups.
rows.note: The paper reports the goodness-of-fit result against an equiprobability hypothesis.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Reported the fraction of retained neurons with a statistically significant local activation–proximity difference.
rows.note: The authors describe local inferential differences as relatively modest.
rows.check: State is judged against the authors' own hypothesis, not any claim version; the link to 'none' is correct. No baseline is given for the 22.8% of neurons significant at the local Kruskal-Wallis test.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Computed Kendall’s τ between activation rank and mean proximity to each of three categorical subdimensions in an average neuron.

conditions.value: exactly 3 taken-clusters, each containing at least 6 tokens

rows.measure: Kendall’s τ between activation rank and dimensional proximity
rows.note: The average neuron was formed by averaging proximity scores across the selected neurons.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Performed PCA on mean core-token proximities to four categorical subdimensions.

conditions.value: exactly 4 taken-clusters, each containing at least 6 tokens

rows.measure: PCA structure and explained variance for the four subdimension-proximity variables
rows.value: Eigenvalues VP1 = 3.74 and VP2 = .19; Factor 1 explains 93.5% of initial variance and Factor 2 explains 4.8%; all subdimensions are positively correlated on Factor 1, while Factor 2 contrasts some subdimensions.
rows.note: The authors interpret the first factor as partial categorical convergence and the second as categorical divergence/polysemy. They report Bartlett p < .0001 and KMO = .82.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Examined activation levels of mean core-tokens projected onto PCA axes for categorical-subdimension proximities.

conditions.value: exactly 4 taken-clusters, each containing at least 6 tokens

rows.measure: Association of token activation with coordinates on the two PCA factors
rows.value: The text reports that higher-activation tokens have the highest positive Factor 1 values and the highest negative Factor 2 values.
rows.note: The authors interpret these positions as associated with greater proximity to more of the categorical subdimensions.
